subject.title: Feature: configurable /new greeting model (or option to suppress greeting)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a typed reset-greeting policy/model override for bare `/new` and `/reset`, and which default should it use across chat and Gateway reset surfaces?
rationale: The remaining work changes compatibility-sensitive reset behavior and provider/model routing, so automation should not choose whether default resets spend a model turn, stay acknowledgement-only, or expose both modes.

options.title: Unified policy with no-model default
options.body: Keep today’s static acknowledgement as the default, then add an explicit opt-in startup/greeting mode and optional cheaper reset-greeting model routing.

options.title: Restore model greeting by default
options.body: Return bare resets to model-generated startup greetings by default and add an explicit static-ack/suppress option for token-conscious users.

options.title: Defer new config
options.body: Keep current acknowledgements and leave reset prompt/model selection unconfigurable until maintainers choose a broader reset-start contract.

recommendation.title: Unified policy with no-model default
recommendation.body: Keep today’s static acknowledgement as the default, then add an explicit opt-in startup/greeting mode and optional cheaper reset-greeting model routing.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the clearest recent reset-contract history and already framed the remaining issue as a maintainer product decision.
